
  The crux of "deeper discovery" is a safety tension: aggressive matching is exactly how an uninstaller nukes the wrong app's data
  (com.acme.foo prefix-matching com.acme.foobar). So the first decision shapes the whole engine:

⏺ User answered Claude's questions:
  ⎿  · How should fuzzy leftover matching trade reclaim against safety? → Owner-aware boundary

⏺ Owner-aware it is - skips com.acme.foobar (different app) and anything a sibling app claims. That same index doubles as the orphan
  finder later.

  Now the safety guards - the real fork is how much they do for you:

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 ☐ Guard action 

When a guard trips (app is running, or it's brew-managed), what should Remove App do?

❯ 1. Warn + one-key act           ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  2. Warn-only (block)            │ "Slack" is running.                                    │
  3. Auto-handle silently         │   [Q] quit & continue   [esc] cancel                   │
                                  │                                                        │
                                  │ "Rectangle" is Homebrew-managed.                       │
                                  │   [B] brew uninstall --cask   [T] trash anyway   [esc] │
                                  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
